addedResources.use: Read Basic Usage, How mup Works Under the Hood, Current Limitations, and Coord Check through Tips for Coord Check at commit 1981497. Use as a design reference, not an installation requirement; skip Wider is Always Better, which is not a finite-run guarantee.

units.title: Parameters, tokens and compute as separate variables, and fixed-token versus fixed-compute contracts
outcomes: Separate parameter count, processed tokens, unique data and arithmetic compute in a run contract.
Derive fixed-token and fixed-compute comparisons with an explicit FLOP-count convention.
Budget memory and elapsed time separately from the arithmetic approximation.
units.why: The LLM Foundations unit on parameter and FLOP counts supplied the arithmetic. Research comparisons now need a contract that says which resource is conserved and which effects remain entangled.

next.note: Use the contract to compare allocation methods rather than slogans.

study.title: CS336 Spring 2026 Assignment 3, Version 26.0.5
study.locator: Section 2.1, Scaling Laws from IsoFLOPs profiles; Section 3.1, Training Run Details
study.depth: Read the API setup as a comparison contract only. Use your existing decoder and corpus locally, not the enrollment-only training service. Never publish assignment solutions.

study.title: Porian et al.: what counts as model size
study.locator: arXiv:2406.19146v1, Sections 2.1 and 2.2, Section 3.2, and Appendix B, Estimating FLOPs and accounting for attention

focus: Use \(N\) for a declared parameter count, \(D\) for processed training tokens and \(C\) for training FLOPs. Unique corpus tokens are a separate quantity when sampling repeats data.
The dense matmul estimate \(C\approx6ND\) is not an identity. Count the output projection even with tied embeddings; account separately for attention, recomputation and other omitted operations.
Fixed tokens asks about capacity at a shared exposure budget. Fixed FLOPs trades capacity against exposure. Fixed unique data permits different repetition counts. None isolates model size by itself.

Keep tokenizer, document split, context, loss denominator, architecture family and tuning budget explicit. Memory depends on microbatch and activations; elapsed time depends on the implementation, not just FLOPs.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, plan dense models with 10 million and 20 million counted parameters. At 2 million processed tokens each, \(6ND\) gives \(1.2\times10^{14}\) and \(2.4\times10^{14}\) FLOPs. At the first compute budget, the larger model instead gets 1 million tokens. Verify with integer arithmetic, then write the analogous two rows for your decoder, including output-head cost, memory state dtypes and omitted FLOPs.
traps: Tied weights reduce stored parameters but do not remove the output matrix multiplication.
Equal optimizer steps do not mean equal tokens if token batch changes. Equal nominal tokens also need the same mask and padding-count policy.
Calling equal elapsed time an IsoFLOP comparison. A kernel improvement can buy more tokens in that time without changing the statistical scaling relationship.

selfTest.q: Under \(C\approx6ND\), what happens to tokens if parameter count doubles at fixed compute?
selfTest.a: They halve. At fixed tokens, the estimated compute instead doubles; these answer different questions.

selfTest.q: Is training twice over a corpus equivalent to a corpus twice as large?
selfTest.a: No. Processed-token count can match while unique data and repetition differ. Record both and evaluate on documents excluded from training.

selfTest.q: Can equal FLOPs guarantee equal peak memory?
selfTest.a: No. State, activations, sequence length, microbatch, precision and recomputation determine peak memory. Measure feasibility separately.

units.stopWhen: Your two comparison tables conserve their declared budgets, and each row names parameter and token conventions plus the main compute and memory omissions.

fit.note: A3 supplies the comparison contract; Porian supplies parameter-count and attention-cost caveats. The mini-project applies them to the existing decoder.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: the lmlab run planner records fixed-token and fixed-compute rows, parameter-count conventions, unique and processed tokens, estimated FLOPs, measured time and peak memory.

units.title: Kaplan scaling, Chinchilla IsoFLOP profiles and why their allocations disagree
outcomes: Derive the allocation implied by a separable parameter-and-token loss model.
Distinguish sampled IsoFLOP minima, fitted valleys and the resulting frontier.
Explain the Kaplan-Chinchilla disagreement using optimization and accounting evidence, not a universal token ratio.
units.why: An allocation rule inherits the experiment that produced it. Separate the empirical frontier from a parametric fit before spending a budget on either.

next.note: Challenge the fitted loss model and its objective.

study.title: Kaplan et al.: historical allocation
study.locator: arXiv:2001.08361v1, Sections 1 and 2, Figure 1, and Section 6, Optimal Allocation of the Compute Budget
study.depth: Section 5 supplies training-time and batch corrections; the allocation conclusion is in Section 6. Read it with Porian below, not as a current prescription.

study.title: Hoffmann et al.: three allocation methods
study.locator: arXiv:2203.15556v1, Figure 1, Sections 3.2 and 3.3, and Appendix D.2, especially Equation 10

study.title: Porian et al.: diagnosing the discrepancy
study.locator: arXiv:2406.19146v1, Figure 1, Sections 3.1 to 3.5 and 5.2

study.title: Besiroglu et al.: Approach 3 replication
study.locator: arXiv:2404.10102v2, Sections 1 to 4 and Appendix A.1

focus: For \(L=E+A N^{-\alpha}+B D^{-\beta}\) with positive coefficients and exponents, substitute \(D=C/(6N)\). The stationary condition is \(\alpha A N^{-\alpha}=\beta B D^{-\beta}\), not equality of the two reducible-loss terms unless the exponents match.
This yields \(N_*=(\alpha A/(\beta B))^{1/(\alpha+\beta)}(C/6)^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)}\). Equal growth follows only when \(\alpha=\beta\). Twenty tokens per parameter is not a universal constant.
Porian isolates output-head FLOPs, excessive warmup and scale-dependent optimizer tuning. Matching decay changes loss but does not by itself explain the allocation gap in that study.
Besiroglu challenges Approach 3 rounding, optimizer termination and intervals using reconstructed data. That does not invalidate the separate IsoFLOP evidence or establish a law for your decoder.
units.reproduce: Derive the stationary condition without notes. As an arithmetic audit, use the rounded Equation 10 constants \(E=1.69\), \(A=406.4\), \(B=410.7\), \(\alpha=0.34\), \(\beta=0.28\) and \(C=5.88\times10^{23}\) FLOPs. Obtain approximately 32.491 billion parameters and 3.01622 trillion tokens; compare with a one-dimensional numerical minimization and require relative allocation error below \(10^{-5}\). This is the rounded published fit, not a recommendation or a reproduction of Chinchilla. Explain the mismatch using Besiroglu.
traps: Fitting a valley when every sampled point is still descending. An optimum outside the sampled range is not identified.
Treating the historical allocation exponents as percentages of actual dollars or wall-clock time.
Repeating the introductory IsoFLOP fixture from the LLM Foundations arithmetic unit and calling it a new measured result.

selfTest.q: Why does the additive floor not change the fixed-compute optimum in this model?
selfTest.a: It is constant in \(N\) and \(D\), so its derivative vanishes. Estimating it can still change the other fitted parameters and hence the estimated optimum.

selfTest.q: What allocation exponents follow from \(\alpha=0.34\) and \(\beta=0.28\)?
selfTest.a: Approximately 0.451613 for parameters and 0.548387 for tokens. They sum to one under \(C=6ND\), but are not both 0.5.

selfTest.q: Does Porian show that decay never matters?
selfTest.a: No. It can improve loss substantially. The claim concerns its limited role in explaining the allocation discrepancy in their tested setups.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Recover an IsoFLOP Compute-Optimal Frontier
practice.locator: Fit a quadratic in \(\log N\) at each compute budget, then a log-space frontier across the recovered minima.
practice.note: Free. The public cases supply square-root and four-tenths-power frontiers with guaranteed interior positive-curvature minima. Add your own boundary-minimum rejection test. These are supplied-data drills, not measured scaling evidence.

units.stopWhen: Your analytic and numerical allocations agree, your frontier code rejects an unsupported valley, and you can explain both the Porian and Besiroglu caveats.

fit.note: The allocation papers, their two critiques and the named free frontier drill cover derivation and preparation without repeating the earlier A3 fixture exercise.

units.title: Irreducible loss, noise floors, and nonlinear versus log-space fitting
outcomes: Implement a positive-coefficient loss model with an explicit additive floor.
Compare raw-loss and log-loss objectives and explain their different error weighting.
Diagnose floor-exponent trade-offs and distinguish an asymptotic loss floor from measurement noise.
units.why: A straight line on log axes can hide a missing additive term. Small fitting choices can reverse the allocation inferred from the same runs.

next.note: Collect configurations that can distinguish the terms you want to fit.

study.title: Hoffmann et al.: the fitted loss surface
study.locator: arXiv:2203.15556v1, Section 3.3, Equations 2 and 3, and Appendix D.2, Equations 10 and 11
study.depth: Use the model and fitting objective, not Appendix D.2 as a proof of separability. Read the Approach 3 caveat below before using its constants.

study.title: Besiroglu et al.: numerical fitting failure
study.locator: arXiv:2404.10102v2, Sections 3.1 and 3.2

study.title: Fit a Data Power Law with a Noise Floor
study.locator: Statement: candidate-floor eligibility, log-space least squares and raw-loss RMSE selection; the three public cases

focus: For \(L(D)=E+A D^{-\alpha}\), only \(\log(L-E)=\log A-\alpha\log D\) is linear. Logging total loss does not remove the floor. A candidate floor must leave positive residual loss.

Raw least squares weights absolute loss errors. For small errors, squared log-loss residuals behave like squared raw errors divided by \(L^2\). Logging the floor-subtracted loss instead gives sensitivity proportional to \(1/(L-E)^2\); these are three different objectives.

An irreducible conditional entropy belongs to a specified tokenizer, context and evaluation distribution. A short sweep cannot establish that a fitted intercept is that entropy. Seed and evaluation noise are variation around measurements, not the intercept.

Use multiple starts, scaled variables, parameter bounds and convergence diagnostics. Save full-precision fits. Besiroglu shows why a solver returning successfully is not enough; Porian also makes optimization quality part of the run contract.
units.reproduce: Construct noiseless losses \(L(D)=1+4D^{-1/2}\) at \(D=1,4,16,64\). Closed-book, recover the floor-subtracted log slope and predict 1.25 at \(D=256\). Fit a no-floor log line to the same observations: its exponent is about 0.289793 and prediction about 0.948683. Then fit the floor, positive coefficient and positive exponent jointly by raw nonlinear least squares from several starts; require maximum absolute fitted-loss error below \(10^{-8}\). Keep the constructed truth separate from your later measured decoder losses.
traps: Calling a fitted floor the entropy of language. Tokenization, context, domain, finite optimization and misspecification all matter.
Silently switching from log total loss to log excess loss. Their noise weighting differs, especially near the floor.
Interpreting a tiny training residual as parameter identifiability. Many floor-exponent combinations can agree over a narrow range.

selfTest.q: Why can a log-log total-loss slope flatten with more data even with a constant true exponent?
selfTest.a: The constant floor contributes more of the total loss. The reducible term still follows its power law, but the total does not.

selfTest.q: Does multiplying an objective by a positive constant change its exact minimizer?
selfTest.a: No. It can change a numerical solver's stopping behavior under absolute tolerances. Check gradients, objective improvement and multi-start agreement rather than relying only on a termination flag.

selfTest.q: Can fixing the floor make an interval look artificially precise?
selfTest.a: Yes. It conditions on a value that may be uncertain or wrong. Profile plausible floors and report how predictions and allocation change.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Fit a Data Power Law with a Noise Floor
practice.locator: Implement the candidate-floor procedure in the statement, not a different joint nonlinear fit.
practice.note: Free. Public cases use inverse-square-root and inverse-linear curves and multiple target sizes. They do not test noisy-run uncertainty. Compare this prescribed fitter with your raw nonlinear fit on the constructed check, then keep both for the mini-project.

units.stopWhen: You pass the named drill, reproduce the missing-floor failure and compare the three objectives without confusing a floor with noise.

fit.note: The paper specifies nonlinear log-loss fitting, the replication diagnoses termination errors, and TensorTonic supplies a distinct candidate-floor implementation contract.

units.title: Identifiable run matrices under a fixed budget and held-out configuration tests
outcomes: Design a sparse matrix that varies capacity and exposure independently enough for the chosen fit.
Run a bounded measured decoder sweep with versioned data, tuning and all-attempt accounting.
Freeze a prediction and acceptance rule before training a configuration excluded from all fitting.
units.why: The fixture has already taught the mechanics. Now the evidence must come from your machine, with enough independent variation to challenge the fit.

next.note: Audit the measured fit before interpreting the held-out result.

study.title: CS336 Spring 2026 Assignment 3: designing a scaling experiment
study.locator: Version 26.0.5, Sections 3.1 and 3.3, problem `scaling_laws`, including the run-selection and predicted-loss questions
study.depth: Replace the enrollment-only service with the local sweep below. The public `test_api.py` and `test_scheduler.py` test the training service itself and need a local PostgreSQL server; they are not an offline fitter test suite. Never publish solutions.

study.title: Porian et al.: grid, tuning and transfer limits
Applied Science Research Laboratory: precommitment and lineage
study.locator: Core requirements; Architecture constraints; Milestones B and C
study.depth: Borrow the experiment protocol only, not the capstone scale or its full experiment program.

focus: Use the tested decoder and versioned corpus from lmlab. In PyTorch 2.14.1, pilot three same-family sizes near 10, 20 and 40 million total parameters at a common context of 128 and three terminal token budgets near 0.25, 0.5 and 1 million. Record actual counts, not size labels.

Reserve a middle-size, middle-token cell before outcomes. Train the other eight cells independently with schedules ending at their own token budgets. Repeat two contrasting fitting cells with three seeds total. Keep one tokenizer, document-disjoint evaluation set, loss mask and loss denominator throughout.

Cap the measured sweep at a few hours using pilot throughput. If CPU-only or memory-limited, shrink all sizes, contexts or token budgets before freezing the matrix. Preserve three sizes and three exposures, record the reduced regime and avoid frontier claims. Count tuning, retries and evaluation in the budget.

For a five-parameter surface, inspect the scaled prediction Jacobian for deficient rank and small singular values. Eight cells do not guarantee practical identifiability. If weak, fit one capacity slice or a simpler local model and report the unresolved terms rather than manufacturing exponents.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, turn your pilot into a run table with planned and actual parameters, processed and unique tokens, token batch, schedule, seeds, estimated FLOPs and measured runtime. Show which rows isolate a size effect, a token effect and a fixed-compute trade-off. Before running the reserved cell, commit its predicted document-held-out loss, uncertainty procedure, tolerance and a plan for a miss. Include a matched-compute pair, adjusting token counts to your actual counted model sizes.
traps: Varying only along one compute contour, then claiming independent capacity and data effects without checking identifiability.
Counting checkpoints from one trajectory as independently trained terminal runs. A schedule designed for the longest run changes the treatment at earlier checkpoints.
Tuning the fit after seeing the reserved loss and still calling the configuration held out. A revised fit needs a new confirmatory configuration.

selfTest.q: Why is holding out documents not the same as holding out a configuration?
selfTest.a: Document holdout tests language-model generalization. Configuration holdout tests the fitted response model on a model-and-token setting it did not use. Both boundaries are needed.

selfTest.q: Can a full-rank Jacobian certify the scaling law?
selfTest.a: No. It is a local identifiability diagnostic under the assumed form and parameter values. Conditioning, noise, optimization and misspecification can still make estimates unstable.

selfTest.q: What should you do when the fitted surface is unstable?
selfTest.a: Report the instability. Narrow the question to an identifiable slice or simpler model, or use the reserved experiment budget to vary the confounded factors. Do not report a precise joint allocation.

units.stopWhen: Your fitting runs are measured and versioned, your fit has a defensible identifiability audit, and the reserved configuration has a committed prediction but has not yet been run.

fit.note: A3 supplies the planning questions; Porian supplies tuning and design limitations; the research-lab protocol and mini-project turn them into an accessible local experiment.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: the lmlab measured run matrix, a matched-compute pair, repeated fitting cells and a configuration-level prediction committed before its training run.

units.title: Fit uncertainty, residual analysis and the influence of failed runs
outcomes: Quantify prediction uncertainty while distinguishing seed variation, evaluation sampling and fit misspecification.
Audit residual structure and influence without silently censoring difficult runs.
Evaluate the frozen held-out configuration and preserve a regime the fitted relationship does not explain.
units.why: A small fitting error is not a trustworthy prediction. The result matters only if it survives the reserved run and the strongest plausible failure analysis.

next.note: Test whether an apparent scale effect is really an optimization mismatch.

study.title: Besiroglu et al.: uncertainty and outliers
study.locator: arXiv:2404.10102v2, Sections 3.1 to 3.3, Figures 3 to 5 and Appendix A.1

study.title: Porian et al.: uncertainty construction
study.locator: arXiv:2406.19146v1, Section 2.3 and Appendix C, Additional data analysis details
study.depth: Distinguish their noise-and-interpolate procedure from resampling independent training seeds. Do not copy its calibrated noise magnitude into your study.

study.title: Applied Science Research Laboratory: failed-run accounting
study.locator: Architecture constraints; Milestones D, E and F; Correctness requirements
study.depth: Apply these to the bounded scaling study, not a new capstone.

focus: The Math Foundations units on resampling and on regression diagnostics supply the tools. Resample the independent unit you actually have. Checkpoints from one run and tokens in one document are not independent seed replicates.

Use the repeated fitting cells to estimate seed variation, with the limitation that it may vary across the matrix. Resample evaluation documents for evaluation uncertainty. A parametric bootstrap can propagate these assumptions through the fitter, but must name the assumed noise model and flag failed refits.

Plot observed-minus-predicted loss against \(N\), \(D\), fitted loss, repetition and optimizer steps. Compare leave-one-configuration-out fits and alternative floors or objectives. Parameter intervals and intervals for a new noisy run answer different questions.

Keep every run and its spent budget. A timeout has no terminal loss at the planned token budget. Exclude invalid measurements by a declared reason; compare fits with and without valid high-loss points. Besiroglu critiques Approach 3 specifically, while Porian shows why optimization mismatches can create structured residuals.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, regenerate your fit from immutable terminal-run records. Add residual plots, leave-one-configuration-out prediction shifts and a seed-noise sensitivity analysis. Confirm the reserved prediction and tolerance were committed first, then train and score that configuration once under the frozen protocol. Report the signed prediction error and whether it meets the declared rule. Preserve one failed regime, such as a pilot with excessive warmup or repeated data; do not promise the failure has a particular loss.
traps: Bootstrapping many checkpoints from a single trajectory and reporting them as many independent experiments.
Assigning a timeout its last partial loss as though it reached the terminal token budget. That changes the predictor and the response together.
Discarding a valid high-loss run because it spoils a power law. It may be the most informative evidence about the law's boundary.

selfTest.q: Does a confidence interval for the fitted mean predict the next training seed?
selfTest.a: Not by itself. A new run adds training-seed and measurement variation. A predictive interval must include the relevant noise and still depends on the assumed response model.

selfTest.q: What can three repeated seeds at two cells establish?
selfTest.a: A limited view of variability at those cells. It does not establish constant variance across all sizes or a reliable tail distribution. Report the sparse replication and use sensitivity analyses.

selfTest.q: The reserved run misses the interval. What follows?
selfTest.a: The frozen procedure failed that check. Audit data lineage, budgets, optimization and model form. Keep the miss; a refit using it becomes exploratory and needs another held-out confirmation.

units.stopWhen: A clean analysis regenerates your uncertainty and residuals, the reserved configuration has an honest pass or miss, and every failed or excluded attempt remains traceable.

fit.note: The replication and Porian supply concrete uncertainty failures and procedures; the laboratory protocol and mini-project supply all-attempt retention and held-out validation.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: residual and influence plots, conditional uncertainty with declared resampling units, the measured held-out prediction error and a retained failure regime.

units.title: Critical batch, learning-rate scaling and the limits of muP width transfer
outcomes: Estimate a target-dependent critical batch from reached runs without treating it as a hardware constant.
Fit local learning-rate and batch trends and test transfer at another width under matched exposure.
Diagnose muP coordinate behavior and distinguish width transfer from depth, data or schedule transfer.
units.why: A small model can look inefficient simply because its batch or warmup is inappropriate. Transfer rules reduce search only when their parameterization and scope are checked.

next.note: Hold optimization steady while changing the training distribution.

study.title: Porian et al.: scale-dependent optimization
study.locator: arXiv:2406.19146v1, Section 3.5, Figure 3 and Appendix E.1 to E.3

study.title: Official muP implementation guide
study.locator: Basic Usage; How mup Works Under the Hood; Current Limitations; Coord Check through Tips for Coord Check
study.depth: Read as a design reference for your existing width-scaling implementation. Skip installation and the legacy loading examples. Read Wider is Always Better as a warning sign to investigate: a reversal at one width and step can also be seed noise, so repeat it before you call the parameterization wrong.

study.title: Estimate Critical Batch Size
study.locator: Statement: reached-target filtering, separate step and example minima, and their ratio

focus: The drill estimates \(B_{\text{crit}}=E_{\min}/S_{\min}\), where examples and steps have separate minima among reached runs. These observed minima approximate limiting quantities; a narrow batch grid can bias the estimate. For language models, declare whether exposure and batch use examples or tokens.

Changing token batch changes the number of updates at fixed exposure. Retune learning rate under the same search budget and keep warmup expressed in a declared unit. Porian also finds the AdamW second-moment coefficient matters at small batches; blindly scaling learning rate is not enough.

The Pretraining Reliability unit on initialization transfer and muP covers the width-scaling rules. The official guide distinguishes hidden matrices, input and readout weights, fixed dimensions and width dimensions. There is no single inverse-width learning-rate rule for every tensor or optimizer.

Coordinate checks should cover initialization and early updates across seeds. Stable activation scales do not guarantee the best learning rate transfers, and width transfer does not license changing depth, tokenizer, sequence length, data distribution or training horizon.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, for reached batches of 8, 16 and 32 examples with 100, 60 and 50 steps, compute consumed examples 800, 960 and 1600; the drill estimate is 16 examples. Then use the smallest two widths of your local decoder with PyTorch 2.14.1: compare a small learning-rate-by-token-batch grid at fixed processed tokens. Record actual updates and warmup tokens. Add initialization and early-update coordinate summaries across three widths and three seeds; compare a predicted transferred learning rate with a neighboring rate at the reserved width. Report whether it transfers, not an expected winning rate.
traps: Treating the batch that fits in memory as the critical batch. Memory capacity and statistical efficiency are different constraints.
Fitting a scaling trend through grid winners at the grid boundary without checking whether the optimum lies outside the grid.

Using the per-matrix learning-rate summary in Section 5 of the Modern LLM Notebook's scaling-laws notebook as a complete muP specification. Use the official parameter-class rules instead; stable coordinates are a diagnostic, not a universal loss guarantee.

selfTest.q: Does the batch with the fewest steps necessarily consume the fewest examples?
selfTest.a: No. In the constructed sweep it takes 50 steps but consumes 1600 examples, while the 100-step run consumes 800. The two minima serve different objectives.

selfTest.q: A batch never reaches the target before the cap. How do you include it?
selfTest.a: Keep it as an unreached, budgeted attempt. Do not use its capped steps as steps-to-target. Report censoring and add an all-unreached guard to your own tests.

selfTest.q: Can flat coordinate scales prove the same learning rate is optimal at every width?
selfTest.a: No. They check scale behavior over the measured widths and early steps. Test the transferred setting against neighboring settings at the new width under the same data and budget.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Estimate Critical Batch Size
practice.locator: Implement the statement's reached-target minima and ratio.
practice.note: Free. Public cases all reach the target and include minima at different batches. Add unreached points and an explicit all-unreached policy in your own tests.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Fit Learning-Rate and Batch-Size Scaling
practice.locator: Select per-scale grid winners, then fit the two specified log-space lines and residuals.
practice.note: Free. Public cases cover exact trends, grid tie order and three-scale residuals. They do not establish transfer from a measured decoder sweep.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Diagnose muP Width Invariants
practice.locator: Fit log-width slopes for activation and update-change RMS and apply the supplied tolerance.
practice.note: Free. Public cases cover constant series, one noninvariant series and small width variation. Keep the actual coordinate and transfer experiment in the section mini-project; supplied arrays are preparation only.

units.stopWhen: You complete the three drills, retain unreached attempts, and distinguish measured coordinate stability from the observed success or failure of learning-rate transfer.

fit.note: Depth failed: the notebook gives overbroad muP rules and the supplied-data drill cannot specify parameter classes. One targeted source pass found the official muP guide; the mini-project supplies measured transfer.

units.title: Mixture response curves, quality versus quantity, repetition and the data-constrained regime
outcomes: Fit source-specific response curves at fixed model size and processed tokens, using realized rather than requested mixture weights.
Separate quality selection from unique-data quantity, repetition and evaluation-domain overlap.
Test a held-out mixture and identify where a single-epoch scaling assumption fails.
units.why: Filtering, mixtures and deterministic shards taught the sampler. The research question is now whether a mixture gain survives exposure matching, domain slices and a new mixture prediction.

next.note: Change when a source is seen and where its examples come from.

study.title: Ye et al.: data mixing response models
study.locator: arXiv:2403.16952v1, Section 3.1 to 3.3, Equations 6 to 8 and Table 1; Appendix A
study.depth: Use the two-domain curve and explicit evaluation-domain aggregation. Skip the large nested extrapolation program in Section 4; validate only within your tested proportions.

study.title: Muennighoff et al.: repeated-data scaling
study.locator: arXiv:2305.16264v5, Sections 3 and 3.1, Sections 5 and 6, and Appendix A
study.depth: Use the effective-data model and the fixed-FLOP repetition comparison. Skip fitting its full effective-parameter extension. The few-epoch finding is specific to the reported GPT-2-style models and C4 experiments, not a safe repetition limit.

focus: At fixed size and exposure, fit each evaluation domain separately, for example \(L_i(r)=c_i+k_i\exp(t_i r)\) for a two-source proportion \(r\). Freeze evaluation token weights before comparing mixtures. A different evaluation mixture changes the objective, not the trained model.

Mixture weights sum to one, so an unrestricted exponential multi-domain model has redundant parameters: a common shift in all \(t_{ij}\) can be absorbed into \(k_i\). Use a reference domain or identifiable contrasts; do not interpret individual coefficients as causal source effects.

Record requested and realized token shares, unique documents, unique token positions, source repetition, sequence lengths and contamination checks. A domain loss gain may be evaluation overlap or concentrated repetition, not improved general data quality.

Compare filtering against both a random subset with the same unique-token budget and the unfiltered pool at the same processed-token budget. Keep tokenizer, model, tuning and held-out documents fixed. More epochs spend real compute even when their effective information gain decays.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, derive the geometric effective-data toy model \(D_{\text{eff}}=U\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-\delta)^j\) for \(m\) complete passes and \(0<\delta<1\). With 100 unique token positions, three passes and \(\delta=0.5\), obtain 175 effective versus 300 processed tokens. This is an assumed decay illustration, not a measured conversion. Then fit a two-domain curve from four measured proportions in lmlab and freeze the prediction at a fifth interior proportion before running it; compare per-domain loss, realized exposure and residuals.
traps: Interpreting TensorTonic's curve across data sizes as a direct fit across mixture proportions. Those are different predictors.
Claiming a higher-quality source wins when it also has more unique tokens, fewer duplicates or more overlap with evaluation.
Treating the repeated-token fit as a guarantee against overfitting. The paper notes failure runs whose increasing held-out loss the saturating formula does not model.

selfTest.q: Domain losses are 2.0 and 2.8 nats per scored token. What is loss with fixed evaluation token shares 25% and 75%?
selfTest.a: 2.6 nats per scored token. This is a token-weighted cross-entropy average with the same tokenizer and scoring policy, not an average of perplexities.

selfTest.q: Can two mixtures trade places as token budget increases?
selfTest.a: Yes. Their floors, coefficients and exponents can differ. The crossing-curve drill illustrates this; predicting the crossing is not evidence until an excluded configuration is measured.

selfTest.q: Why does the geometric effective-token sum saturate?
selfTest.a: For \(0<\delta<1\), the ratio \(1-\delta\) is below one, so the infinite sum is \(U/\delta\). This follows from the assumed decay rule, not from a universal law of repeated text.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Extrapolate Data-Mixture Scaling Curves
practice.locator: Fit one candidate-floor power law across data sizes per named mixture, then compare target predictions.
practice.note: Free. Public cases include crossing curves, mixture-index ties and three fitted mixtures. Add uncertainty and measured proportions in the mini-project: use a small fixed decoder and the existing two source corpora, hold one proportion out, and compare a repeated subset against fresh data at matched processed tokens. Shrink the token budget on CPU before freezing the protocol.

units.stopWhen: Your named drill passes, the measured mixture prediction has a recorded error, and your quality and repetition comparisons retain unique-token counts and fixed evaluation weights.

fit.note: Ye supplies per-domain response curves; Datablations supplies repetition and its failure boundary; TensorTonic and the mini-project provide separate supplied-data and measured practice.

units.title: Curriculum, mid-training and annealing, and synthetic-data gains and collapse risk
outcomes: Separate a late data-distribution change from learning-rate annealing with a matched continuation experiment.
Audit synthetic examples for teacher dependence, verification, diversity and evaluation leakage.
Explain recursive replacement collapse without claiming that every use of generated data must fail.
units.why: A curriculum changes the order of exposure, not just its total. OLMo 2 provides a concrete late-stage recipe; recursive-data experiments show why a synthetic source needs more than a good average score.

next.note: Turn the bounded evidence into a budget choice with explicit limits.

study.title: OLMo 2: annealing and targeted data
study.locator: arXiv:2501.00656v3, Sections 4.1 to 4.5, especially 4.4.2, Evaluating Math Data with Microanneals
study.depth: Read checkpoint soups as an additional experimental cost and confound. Do not reproduce the large-model training or paid synthetic-data generation; use your small decoder and a bounded local source.

study.title: Shumailov et al.: recursive replacement and its assumptions
study.locator: arXiv:2305.17493v3, Section 3, What is model collapse?, and Sections 4.1 and 4.2, including the single-dimensional Gaussian example
study.depth: Keep the finite-sample recursive model separate from claims about verified synthetic math. Stop before the later large-language-model experiments; the Gaussian loop is the CPU reproduction.

focus: The Pretraining Reliability unit on warmup-stable-decay schedules covers the schedule mechanics. From one checkpoint including optimizer state, cross original versus targeted data with unchanged versus annealed learning rate. Match continuation tokens and use the same seed list; score both general and target domains.

To test order rather than composition, compare a shuffled fixed mixture with a staged schedule using the same source-token totals. The four-way continuation separates local schedule and data effects but does not alone establish that late exposure is better than early exposure.

For synthetic data, record the teacher or generator version, prompts, sampling settings, verification rule, rejection rate, accepted diversity and total generation cost. Freeze evaluation before generation and check both prompt and answer overlap. A verifier can select its own blind spots.

Recursive replacement can lose support and amplify sampling or approximation error. Fresh real-data replay, accumulation rather than replacement, external verification and teacher quality change the process. Neither a successful targeted rewrite nor a collapse toy establishes a universal scaling law.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, implement a NumPy recursive Gaussian fit-generate-refit loop from a standard normal, using 32 samples per generation, 100 generations and seeds 0 through 19. Compare replacement-only fitting with a control that draws fresh standard-normal samples every generation. Track fitted mean, variance and the probability mass outside the original interval \([-2,2]\). Name whether variance uses `ddof=0` or `ddof=1`; the MLE conditional expectation multiplies variance by \(31/32\), whereas the unbiased estimator does not have that conditional mean shrinkage. Individual trajectories need not shrink monotonically. Then write the four matched local-decoder continuation rows before training any of them.
traps: Crediting a new mixture for a gain while also changing the schedule, checkpoint selection or model soup. These interventions require separate accounting.

Reading the \(1-q\) in collapse v3 Section 4.1 as the chance of losing an event in one generation. It is the probability of losing it at some point in the recursion, since the chain ends on that state with probability \(q\); one generation of \(M\) independent draws misses it with probability \((1-q)^M\).
Saying unbiased sample variance prevents recursive collapse. Conditional unbiasedness is not a guarantee about a typical long recursive path or preservation of support.

selfTest.q: Why branch every continuation from the same complete checkpoint?
selfTest.a: It fixes the starting weights and optimizer history. Otherwise a data or schedule effect can be a different starting state or a reset-state effect. Record any intentionally reset state as another intervention.

selfTest.q: What would establish a local data-by-schedule interaction?
selfTest.a: The targeted-minus-original data difference changes between the two schedules beyond the declared uncertainty. Report all four cells and their domain slices rather than only the winning continuation.

selfTest.q: Does the Gaussian toy contradict useful synthetic math data in OLMo 2?
selfTest.a: No. The toy studies finite-sample recursive fitting under explicit replacement rules. OLMo 2 uses targeted data, mixed sources and a different training process. Its result is evidence for that recipe, not protection against every recursive-data failure.

units.stopWhen: Your diagnostic distinguishes estimator bias from recursive path behavior, and the matched continuations separate data, schedule and their interaction without hiding general-domain regressions.

fit.note: OLMo 2 supplies the concrete curriculum case; the collapse paper supplies a bounded counterexample and CPU diagnostic. The mini-project supplies matched continuation practice without paid generation.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: a CPU recursive-data diagnostic and four short continuations of the smallest existing decoder, crossing schedule and data while retaining general-domain loss. Use locally generated or already available licensed synthetic text, not a paid teacher API; cap generation and continuation time during the pilot.

units.title: Confounded scaling gains, inference-aware scaling and the budget allocation decision
outcomes: Separate statistical scaling gains from architecture, tokenizer, optimizer, implementation and evaluator changes.
Choose a next model, token or mixture experiment using measured uncertainty and total research cost.
State the supported range and a decisive falsification test for the resulting budget recommendation.
units.why: The deliverable is not an exponent. It is a defensible change in what you train next, including the case where uncertainty makes another measurement worth more than a larger run.

next.note: Carry the matched-budget and no-training baseline discipline into adaptation.

study.title: Optional: lifetime compute versus serving cost
study.locator: arXiv:2401.00448v3, Section 2 (Equation 3), Sections 3 and 4 (47 trained models up to 10,000 tokens per parameter) and Section 6 (Equation 6)
study.depth: Optional serving extension. Equations 3 and 6 are conditional cost models: their answers depend on the assumed demand, utilization and prices, not on your hardware. Skip Appendix A and do not inherit the rounded Chinchilla coefficients as a local fit.

focus: Use the measured fixed-token and matched-compute comparisons, held-out error and retained failure regime. State tokenizer and evaluator identity before comparing loss; changed tokens or scoring denominators can make numerical losses incomparable.

A kernel change can improve elapsed-time allocation without changing loss per processed token. An architecture change can alter both FLOPs and the fitted response. A larger hyperparameter search can move the apparent frontier while spending unreported compute. Keep search, pilot, failed-run and evaluation costs in the ledger.

Compare the next capacity increase, more tokens, a mixture change and a replication run. Report predicted gain with sensitivity to floor, objective and noisy cells; include feasibility and the cost of being wrong. Choose another measurement when plausible fits reverse the decision.

Optional: with the simplified dense convention, lifetime FLOPs are \(C_{\text{life}}=6ND_{\text{train}}+2ND_{\text{infer}}\). This omits important context and attention costs. Prompt processing and autoregressive decoding have different utilization, so FLOPs alone do not price a service or prove a latency target.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, regenerate your study tables and plots from terminal records, then write a one-page budget decision naming the winning action, its uncertainty, the held-out miss or success, one failed regime and the scale or data boundary beyond which you will not use the fit. Optional arithmetic audit: suppose equal useful quality has been established separately for a 20M-parameter model trained on 1M tokens and a 10M-parameter model trained on 3M tokens. Under the stated dense convention their training costs are \(1.2\times10^{14}\) and \(1.8\times10^{14}\) FLOPs; the smaller model recovers the extra training cost at 3M lifetime inference tokens. Check equality at that demand. These constructed rows do not establish equal quality or equal dollar cost.
traps: Selecting the most confident-looking fit rather than the one whose held-out prediction and residuals survive the protocol.
Spending all remaining compute on the nominal optimum when a cheap repeated cell could distinguish opposite recommendations.
Reading Sardana's Section 6 cost optimum as a measured price. It rests on assumed utilization, hardware and request mix; the paper's experiments test only the loss side, at its own model scale.

selfTest.q: A faster kernel yields lower loss in the same hour. Is that a new statistical scaling law?
selfTest.a: Not by itself. It may allow more tokens or search within the hour. Compare at matched tokens and matched counted compute as well as elapsed time, and identify which budget the recommendation conserves.

selfTest.q: Two plausible fits recommend different model sizes. What is the next decision?
selfTest.a: Choose a feasible measurement that separates their predictions or reduces influential noise, and freeze its decision rule. Report that the current allocation is not identified rather than averaging the recommendations without justification.

selfTest.q: Why can a smaller model trained longer be attractive for deployment?
selfTest.a: Extra training cost can be amortized over lower per-token serving cost if it reaches the required quality. Demand, prompt and output lengths, batching, memory and latency constraints can change the result; the training-only optimum is a different objective.

units.stopWhen: A clean rerun regenerates the evidence, your decision changes a named budget allocation, and another reader can see what would overturn it and where it must not be extrapolated.

fit.note: Porian and the laboratory supply confound and decision discipline. Sardana supplies the optional lifetime-cost objective, not a frontier-scale validation claim; no additional resource is needed.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: the final bounded budget decision, all-attempt cost ledger, clean regeneration, skeptical confound audit and next decisive experiment. If taking the optional serving extension, measure prompt and decode time separately on the existing small models and fixed local prompts; record hardware, precision, batch and context instead of borrowing a paper's utilization or prices.
